name: Glendo State Park (Whiskey Gulch Campground)
note: Whiskey Gulch is a large campground strung along about half a mile of Glendo Reservoir's south shore, entered directly off Glendo Park Road, with the park's Whiskey Gulch high- and low-water boat ramps. Most sites lie among or behind the cottonwoods and willows that line the shore and flood at high water; sites 13 and 14, on an open point, come closest to the lake, and as the reservoir draws down later in summer the water recedes across bare flats. --Claude

Wyoming State Parks' own Whiskey Gulch page (wyoparks.wyo.gov/index.php/about-our-campgrounds/1715-whiskey-gulch-glendo, read as search-result text 2026-11-20; the site refuses with an F5 challenge) and its copies on The Dyrt (thedyrt.com/camping/wyoming/whiskey-gultch) and Campflare (read 2026-11-20): 'Whiskey Gulch is a large campground, which can be accessed directly off of Glendo Park Road'; 'Almost all campsites in Whiskey Gulch are at least partially shaded, with the exceptions of sites 11 through 13 and sites 23 through 25'; 'gravel sites with picnic tables and fire pits, plus one concrete pad site'; 'There are 29 campsites'; high- and low-water boat ramps with courtesy docks; Pine Knob Shelter (first-come) at the centre and the reservable Whiskey Gulch Group Shelter at the west end. No 4WD, sand or rig-size wording in the park text (checked first, per leads 15/23); a 2025-10-29 Dyrt review: 'Easy access from the highway paved roads all the way', and 2026-08-31: 'the gravel road is mostly smooth ... a little washout in some areas'. Imagery 2026-11-20: gravel loop roads with pull-through and back-in spurs on three lobes of the shore, toilet buildings and shelters, matching the engine's unit points. Not in the DB: no WY 'Whiskey' name match; within 3 km only Glendo entries, none with FacilityId 349 - 15741 Mule Hill (FacilityId 339; its MH08/MH09 ~0.5 km NW of WG28), 15743 Sagebrush (FacilityId 342; SB20 ~0.2 km SE of WG01), 13969 Custer Cove (336) 1.6 km N across the water, 15744 Shelter Point (345) 1.7 km E, 13977 Reno Cove (341) 3.0 km. Sagebrush's park text says it 'connects with Shelter Point and Whiskey Gulch campgrounds' - neighbouring, each its own engine facility. Public (state): no price gate.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-20: Esri World Imagery and USGS 3DEP (elevation.nationalmap.gov 3DEPElevation exportImage, F32) fetched in the identical EPSG:3857 square frame at 500 m (0.91 m/px) and four 120 m (0.24 m/px) half-widths, with every reserve.wyoming.gov unit point (grid MapInfo, FacilityId 349) plotted and the full-pool contour drawn; all images rendered. Imagery is drawn down and leaf-off (the shore 30-60 m lakeward of the full-pool line). Glendo full pool 4635.0 ft = 1413.51 m NAVD88 (glendo_notes.txt); lidar hydro-flattened water 1412.98 m. Unit points (lidar m) and nearest full-pool crossing of the connected reservoir surface: WG01 1417.9, 16 m; WG02 1418.1, 27 m; WG03 1416.2, 19 m; WG04 1416.1, 22 m; WG05 1416.0, 31 m; WG06 1419.0, 56 m; WG07 1415.8, 24 m; WG08 1417.6, 41 m; WG09 1415.3, 14 m; WG10 1415.6, 8 m; WG11 1418.5, 32 m; WG12 1424.3, 93 m; WG13 1414.3, 6-7 m; WG14 1418.2, 17 m (its paved ADA pad 1418.3 m, 17 m); WG15 1417.2, 16 m; WG16 1418.9, 53 m; WG17 1418.3, 59 m; WG18 1417.4, 19 m; WG19 1417.4, 25 m; WG20 1416.6, 31 m; WG21 1416.0, 38 m; WG22 1415.4, 18 m; G23 1417.3, 54 m; G24 1415.1, 16 m; WG26-WG30 1415.4-1418.1, 37-74 m. Ground check: WG13 sits on an open gravel/sand clearing at the tip of the central point, 0.8 m above full pool, with the full-pool line 6-7 m north (profiles N/NE/NW: 1414.3 -> 1414.0 at 5 m -> water surface at 10 m) over open sand with a few single cottonwoods; the gravel turnaround around the tip lies below full pool (flooded at high water), so nothing stands between the pad and the high-water edge. WG14 (with WG14's concrete ADA pad beside it) sits on an open grass slope just south of WG13, 4.7 m above full pool, falling evenly (1418.2 -> 1417.5 -> 1416.1 -> 1414.7 -> water at 20 m) to the open cove west of the point, with no treeline, road or bank between - walk-across, not a cut bank. Every other lakeward site (WG01-WG04, WG07, WG09, WG10, WG15, WG18-WG22, G24) ends at the inland edge of a dense, continuous cottonwood/willow stand 30-60 m deep, with the full-pool line running inside the trees; park text (via The Dyrt/Campflare copies): 'During high water, the lowest cottonwoods and willows flood' -> water among the trunks, filtered view at most (15741 Mule Hill / 15740 Indian Point precedent); WG15 looks onto a narrow tree-filled arm of the gulch. -> two clear waterfront sites (WG13, WG14) within ~20 m of full pool over open ground -> lakefront with a caveat naming them (few-clear-sites rule, AWH 2026-11-10; 15743 Sagebrush SB01/SB02 precedent); the drawdown apron counts because these pads sit at the full-pool line (13969 Custer Cove precedent). Engine tags every Whiskey Gulch camping unit 'Waterfront Setting: Reservoir' (type-level). Not below the dam: the campground is on the reservoir's south shore, ~2.5 km west of the dam.
